comment: Bytes, measured over the **production** build, which is the one that ships and the one `gates:size` now makes for itself in reports/size/production/. A budget here moves DOWN only (AGENTS.md section 11, ADR-0003 decision 5); raising one is a commit that says why, inside the diff the reviewer reads. The byte count is no longer the only instrument over this build: scripts/gates/module-manifest.json lists which modules each bundle contains, and that list is what now catches a module arriving. || MEASURED. Set on 2026-09-13 from a production build at main.cjs 1078, preload.cjs 547, renderer.js 649, index.html 898, renderer.css 1313 — total 4485, reproduced in this lane rather than taken from the record that carried them. index.html and renderer.css are copied rather than bundled and are byte-identical in both build modes. Every number was checked against the file on disk and against esbuild's own `metafile.outputs[...].bytes`, which at the pinned esbuild 0.28.2 are equal for all three bundles in both modes; the budgets compare the file on disk, because that is what a distributable is and it stays the right quantity if esbuild ever changes what it counts. || MARGIN. Four of the five budgets are their measured size plus one kibibyte, rounded up to the next whole kibibyte, so the real margin is between 1024 and 2047 bytes per file. Under the previous weighing that margin was sized against documentation, because the development build keeps doc comments and the bound that mattered was the largest doc block in the project, RowFlag's clip-bit documentation at 1748 source bytes. **That bound is gone**: this build is minified, so a doc comment costs a bundle nothing at all and no margin has to absorb one. What the margin is sized against now is ordinary code. Measured 2026-09-13 by building each module on its own and reading its metafile attribution, one line of this project's code costs between 4.9 and 19.9 production bytes — 19.9 in src/ui/renderer.ts, 17.3 in src/app/window.ts, 13.0 in src/contracts/commit-columns.ts — so a kilobyte of margin is between 50 and 200 lines of new code, which is a slice's worth and not an edit's. What this margin does NOT catch is what it never caught: the failure it was set after, the unread contract ring returning to both shell bundles, is +76 production bytes and passes here with room to spare. That is now the module manifest's job and not this file's, and a reader who expects the byte count to see it will be wrong. || RENDERER HEADROOM, which is an initial budget and is labelled as one. renderer.js is a stub awaiting E01-M01-S05, so its measured 649 bytes are not a size this rule can add a margin to; the steady-state rule would give 2048, and a budget whose first act is to be raised teaches that budgets are for raising. The precedent is ADR-0002 decision 6, which sets ten budgets over an application that does not exist and says: 'These are the initial budgets. S07 of the first milestone calibrates them by measuring the assembled application on the development machine and commits the baselines.' E01-M01-S07 is budgets, baselines and render stability, and **this budget is calibrated there**, so the movement expected of it is DOWNWARD at calibration rather than upward at S05. It is not exempt from the ratchet and must not be read as though it were: if it ever has to move outward it moves in an argued commit like any other. The 12288 is derived, and here is the derivation, measured in this lane. The floor: a stand-in consumer built outside this repository that only reads the existing decode API and the flag constants — no row pool, no canvas, no markup — costs 1745 production bytes, of which 1320 are the contract modules it pulls in (commit-columns 793, refs 147, column-read 143, result 127, layout 98, bridge 21, index 0) and 425 its own body; a second stand-in that also calls the bridge and names the channels costs 2465. The rate: 19.9 production bytes per line of code, the densest of the nine modules measured above and the one that is browser-targeted renderer code. The estimate, which is an inference and is labelled as one: a renderer meeting ADR-0002 decision 5 — a fixed pool of recycled rows moved by transform, one viewport-sized canvas redrawn from the layout buffers under a coalesced animation frame, devicePixelRatio scaling, arithmetic hit-testing, and the scroll and resize handling around them — is about 500 lines of code, which at 19.9 bytes a line is 9950 bytes; 9950 above the 1320-byte floor is 11270, and the next whole kibibyte is 12288. || TOTAL. The five budgets sum to 22528 and the total is 20480, which is below that sum, and the property it buys is narrower than it used to be. It cannot be a second constraint on renderer.js: 12288 of the total is that file's initial allocation and has to stay whole, because a total that fired when S05 filled a budget S05 was given would be an unstated second renderer budget, which is exactly the trap this file was just repaired for. So the total is a second constraint on the other four. Their measured sizes sum to 3836 and their margins are 1994, 1501, 1150 and 1759; the total leaves them 8192, of which 4356 is margin, so any TWO of the four may spend their full margin at once and any three may not. When E01-M01-S07 calibrates renderer.js downward, this number comes down with it in the same commit. || WHAT THIS MEASURES, and what it stopped measuring. It measures the bundles a user would receive. Until 2026-09-13 it measured the development build in dist/, on the reasoning — which was sound when it was written, and is kept here so that a reader can check the change — that unminified is the stricter of the two measurements and needs no second build. Both halves were true. What review round 11 measured is that 'stricter' meant stricter about comments: the same three bundles are 1.9x to 2.6x larger unminified (2173 against 1078, 1402 against 547, 1215 against 649), almost all of it doc comments, and a stand-in renderer that merely reads the decode API measured 7232 development bytes against a 3072 budget in this lane — over its whole budget before a line of rendering exists, entirely from prose. A gate that prices documentation against a bundle's budget pays an author to delete it, in a project whose discipline is writing it down, and gates:contract records shapes rather than text so nothing else would have objected. Nothing ships the development build, so the budget now weighs the one that does. The measurements behind the decision are in ADR-0003 section 2, gate 11, and in docs/plan/E01-commit-graph/M01-first-graph/S01-scaffold-and-contract.md.
